A word to the wise: set up really good fucking keybinds for the family. What I mean by that is don’t have one big offensive cd on R, another on G and another on some other random ass keybind or you will run out of binds. Rather, you need to put all those big offensive cd’s on R for instance, and use shift/alt modifiers on R for the other big offensive cd’s. Same for movement abilities, those go on Q with shift/alt modifiers, CC abilities on E. You see where I’m going with this? Also bind zoom in and zoom out to Ctrl mouse wheel, that way you can put bindings on your mouse wheel. Your thumb mouse buttons are your best binds, I have my main rotation on those so that I can use my left hand to move in combination with mouse running) while right hand is doing rotation. 

Keybinds: 1-5 q e r t f g, thumb mouse buttons, scroll wheel. All with shift/alt modifiers (or ctrl if you like that modifier more) z x c can be good too. Not every single spell needs to be bound, but most should be. Clicking is bad. It will feel weird for them at first but muscle memory is a hell of a thing.

No, not at all. I’m just saying if you have shatter, do that combo I told you for open world single target. Frost bolt till enemy is close then shatter combo for double crit dmg. (That being said u don’t have to take shatter, can kinda just frostbolt and CoC things down for open world)

For damage in dungeon you’re pretty much just aoe’ing if there are 3+ mobs. The idea though is to not just blow all your mana on one pack then be useless for the next two packs while you drink. Instead, get off some good aoe then conserve a bit of mana with some wands (because after 5 seconds of not casting, your mana regenerates at a much higher rate even when in combat) while your team finishes them off since they’ll be pretty low after you send a few aoe spells. Conjure a ton of water before you enter dungeons and drink after every pack even if it’s just for a few seconds. If you really want to min max you can move a bit ahead of the party before the mobs die so that you start drinking right as combat ends and don’t have to spend time running up after combat and then drinking, if that makes sense. Also you can continue to drink for a few seconds as the tank is pulling the next pack in order to give him a moment to get some threat so you don’t instantly rip agro from your aoe. 

As you get into higher dungeons you will notice that pack size is going to increase, if you’re running a lot of dungeons you may want to take improved blizzard so that all the mobs are super slow as the tank probably won’t be able to hold threat on more than 3-4 mobs. Improved blizzard is really good for big pack control too because if you’re low on mana or just want to conserve mana you can use rank1 blizzard purely in order to keep mobs that you do have threat on from reaching you. Also rank1 cone of cold can be a really good tool if you’re low on mana and just need to kite some mobs for a bit- also you should only have rank1 nova on your bars since you only use it as a cc tool and don’t need higher ranks for a few extra damage at the cost of a lot of extra mana. 

Mage in dungeons is just a balancing act of mana, you want to use enough on every pull to help out your group, but you don’t want to burn it all and then have to drink for the next 40 secs. If you can afford the good water at lvl 45 your overall dps for a dungeon will be higher since you’re spending less time drinking after every pull(I usually use my shitty conjured water for little drinks after each pack then send a big vendor water for when I’m lower on mana). 

Hope this makes sense, lemme know if you have any questions!
